intro: A categorical sample can be produced by adding Gumbel noise to logits and taking an argmax. Supplied uniforms make every choice reproducible for inspection.
task: Use the supplied uniform draws to perturb logits. Compare a deterministic preference with a noise-driven change of action.
requirements: logits and uniforms are matching nonempty vectors. Every uniform must lie strictly between zero and one.

Subtract max(logits) from the logits first, then compute scores=shifted_logits-log(-log(uniforms)). Return the integer index of the largest score, breaking exact ties toward the lowest index. Centering preserves small noise differences beside a huge common logit offset.
Do not apply softmax before adding noise, divide by temperature, or generate new random numbers. The inputs supply one uniform draw per category.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Watch both logarithms
hints.body: The inner logarithm is negative; negate it before taking the outer logarithm.

hints.title: Logit shifts do not change the choice
hints.body: Adding the same constant to every logit shifts all perturbed scores equally.

explanation: Independent uniform draws transformed as -log(-log(U)) have a standard Gumbel distribution. Adding them to logits yields a sample with probabilities proportional to exponentiated logits.
With fixed supplied draws this function is deterministic. It exposes the sampling mechanism; a single outcome does not estimate a category probability.
